findings.title: Resolve removes live links and serves expired ones
findings.description: The expiration test is inverted: DateTime.Now < link.ExpiresAt is true for every valid, unexpired link, so the first redirect removes the link and returns 404. Links whose expiry has already passed are instead returned and hit-counted.

findings.title: BearerToken throws on empty or malformed Authorization headers
findings.description: BearerToken unconditionally returns parts[1] from header.Split(' '). Program.Handle calls it for every request, and an empty header produces a one-element array, so every unauthenticated request throws IndexOutOfRangeException before the 401 response can be written.

findings.title: Discarded handler tasks leave requests without any response
findings.description: Task.Run(() => Handle(context)) is neither awaited nor wrapped in a try/catch. Exceptions such as FormatException, IndexOutOfRangeException, KeyNotFoundException, and DivideByZeroException become unobserved task faults, leaving the HttpListener response open and the client without an HTTP response.

findings.title: First link creation always fails with KeyNotFoundException
findings.description: Create reads quota[owner] before that owner has ever been inserted into the dictionary. The dictionary indexer throws KeyNotFoundException on the first link for each owner; Program.Links only catches ArgumentException, so valid POST /links requests fault.

findings.title: Page asks GetRange for one item more than the list contains
findings.description: When size exceeds the remaining number of links, end is set to all.Count + 1, and GetRange(offset, end - offset) requests all.Count + 1 - offset elements. With the default size of 20 on a fresh store, GET /links throws instead of returning a page. Negative offset or size also reaches GetRange without validation.

findings.title: Stats divides by zero on an empty store
findings.description: store.TotalHits() / store.Count throws DivideByZeroException whenever no links exist. This is the normal state of a freshly started server, so /stats faults instead of returning zeroes.

findings.title: Default report writes one file but reads another
findings.description: Export.ExportCsv substitutes 'links' when name is empty, but Report passes the original empty name to Export.ReadReport, which reads '.csv'. A /report request without an explicit name therefore throws FileNotFoundException and returns 500 after successfully writing links.csv.

findings.title: Malformed ttl query crashes link creation
findings.description: int.Parse(query['ttl']) is evaluated before the try block. A nonnumeric or out-of-range ttl throws FormatException or OverflowException, which is not converted to the intended 400 response.

findings.title: Malformed or negative pagination query crashes listing
findings.description: offset and size are parsed with int.Parse without a try/catch, and negative values are passed straight to Store.Page. Bad query values produce an unhandled FormatException, OverflowException, or ArgumentOutOfRangeException rather than a 400 response.

findings.title: Validate always succeeds and startup ignores its result
findings.description: Validate only logs detected problems and unconditionally returns true; Program.cs line 20 also discards the returned value. Invalid ports, negative cache sizes, and nonpositive timeouts therefore proceed into HttpListener and Cache construction instead of failing at startup.

findings.title: Utilization reports only 0 or 100 and divides by zero
findings.description: entries.Count / limit * 100 is integer division, so a half-full cache reports 0 and only a completely full cache reports 100. If a configured limit of zero reaches Utilization, it also throws DivideByZeroException on /stats.

findings.title: SuccessRate collapses every partial percentage to zero
findings.description: used / links.Count * 100 uses integer division. If one of two links has hits, /stats reports success_rate 0 instead of 50; the only nonzero value is 100 when every link has hits.

findings.title: Verify never expires sessions
findings.description: Verify returns a matching session without comparing ExpiresAt to the current time. Tokens issued with Issue remain accepted indefinitely, expired sessions are never removed here, and the sessions dictionary can grow without bound as tokens are issued.

findings.title: RequireAdmin accepts every role
findings.description: The method returns true when the role is admin or owner, but its final statement also returns true for every other role. The documented admin-only check therefore never denies a session.

findings.title: Invalid LINKD_PORT replaces the default with zero
findings.description: int.TryParse(port, out cfg.Port) assigns zero to cfg.Port when parsing fails. The service then starts with port zero instead of preserving the documented default of 8080, and Validate does not reject the bad configuration.

findings.title: Bad LINKD_TIMEOUT_MS overwrites the default with zero
findings.description: When int.TryParse fails, out variable ms is zero and the log says the default is kept, but cfg.Timeout is still assigned TimeSpan.FromMilliseconds(0). The result is a zero timeout rather than the 10-second default.

findings.title: Millisecond cache TTL is interpreted as seconds
findings.description: The method documents LINKD_CACHE_TTL_MS as milliseconds but calls TimeSpan.FromSeconds(n). A value of 300 produces a five-minute TTL instead of 300 milliseconds, retaining stale cache entries for 1000 times too long.

findings.title: LINKD_FETCH_LIMIT is parsed but never applied
findings.description: The successful branch contains the no-op parsed = parsed and never assigns cfg.FetchLimit. Environment configuration for this field is silently ignored and FetchLimit remains 32.

findings.title: LoadFile silently ignores all file read errors
findings.description: catch (Exception) suppresses permission errors, invalid paths, and I/O failures as well as the documented missing-file case. raw stays empty, so the service starts with defaults and no indication that the requested configuration was not applied.

findings.title: Invalid cache_size in a config file aborts config loading
findings.description: int.Parse(value) throws FormatException or OverflowException for nonnumeric or oversized cache_size values. Unlike missing files, this parse error is not handled and propagates out of LoadFile.

findings.title: Link creation response can emit invalid JSON
findings.description: target and code are interpolated directly into a JSON string. A target supplied through a percent-encoded query can contain a double quote or backslash, producing malformed JSON that clients cannot parse.

findings.title: Redirect lowercases codes that the store permits
findings.description: Store.ValidateCode accepts uppercase letters, and ImportAll or Rename can store mixed-case codes, but /l always calls code.ToLower() before Resolve. Those stored codes can never be resolved through the redirect endpoint.

findings.title: Links listing returns only a count, not the page contents
findings.description: The endpoint calls store.Page(offset, size) but discards the returned Link objects except for Count. Clients receive 'N link(s)' with no codes, targets, owners, or expiry information, so the listing does not return the requested page.

findings.title: Admin quotas endpoint returns owner count instead of quotas
findings.description: store.Quotas().Count is the number of keys in the quota dictionary, not the per-owner link counts that the endpoint documents. An admin receives one aggregate number and cannot see any owner's quota.

findings.title: Peek treats expired entries as present
findings.description: Peek only calls entries.ContainsKey(code) and never checks Entry.Expires. Cache.Warm therefore skips refreshing a code whose cached value has expired until Get or a separate sweep removes it, leaving stale entries eligible to be treated as warm.

findings.title: Cache eviction is not LRU and fails at zero limit
findings.description: Set picks entries.Keys.First(), ignoring the Entry.Used field, so it does not evict the least recently used entry. It also evicts an unrelated entry when merely updating an existing code at capacity. With limit <= 0, First() on an empty dictionary throws InvalidOperationException.

findings.title: CSV fields are written without escaping
findings.description: Code, target, owner, and hits are interpolated into comma-separated rows without quoting. Owner and target values can contain commas, quotes, or newlines, which shifts columns or creates extra rows in the exported report.

findings.title: Async export is unawaitable and writes only a header
findings.description: ExportCsvAsync is async void, so callers cannot await completion or catch write failures. It also ignores the links parameter and writes only 'code,target', producing an incomplete report; an empty name is not normalized to 'links' as in the synchronous exporter.

findings.title: Report writers leak handles when a write fails
findings.description: ExportCsv and ArchiveAll create StreamWriter instances and call Close only on the success path. If writer.Write throws, Close is skipped and the file handle remains open until finalization.

findings.title: Rename validates the source code twice and never validates the destination
findings.description: Both calls are ValidateCode(from). The to value is never length- or character-checked, and a null destination reaches links.ContainsKey(to), so invalid or null destination codes can be stored or cause ArgumentNullException.

findings.title: Delete does not restore the owner's quota slot
findings.description: Delete removes the link but leaves quota[link.Owner] incremented. The method's documented behavior of giving an owner their quota slot back is not implemented, so repeated create/delete cycles keep increasing the reported link count.

findings.title: Top returns the least-followed links first
findings.description: The sort comparator a.Hits.CompareTo(b.Hits) orders hits ascending, and Take(n) then selects the front of that list. The method returns the least followed links instead of the most followed links.

findings.title: ByOwner matches substrings instead of exact owners
findings.description: l.Owner.Contains(owner) returns links owned by ann when owner is an, and an empty owner matches every string. The method does not return links belonging to exactly the requested owner as documented.

findings.title: Extend resets expiry from now and revives dead links
findings.description: Extend assigns DateTime.Now.Add(ttl) rather than adding ttl to the existing ExpiresAt, so it can shorten a long lifetime and does not push expiry out by the requested amount. It also gives an already-expired link a new future expiry, contradicting the documented finality of expiry.

findings.title: Quotas returns the live dictionary instead of a snapshot
findings.description: Quotas returns the internal quota object. Any caller can add, remove, or alter owner counts, directly changing store state even though the method documents that mutations must not affect the store.

findings.title: ImportAll is not atomic
findings.description: Each link is validated and immediately inserted inside the same loop. If a later batch item has an invalid code, earlier items remain in links, violating the documented guarantee that a failed batch leaves the store untouched.

findings.title: Prune returns the remaining count instead of the removed count
findings.description: Prune carefully increments removed but returns links.Count. Callers asking how many links were removed receive the number still stored; pruning every link returns 0 even though many were removed.

findings.title: Janitor bypasses Delete and leaves quota counts inflated
findings.description: The janitor removes expired links directly through store.All().Remove(code), so the per-owner quota entry created by Create is never decremented. Expired links disappear from links while Quotas and CountForOwner continue reporting them.

findings.title: WarmCache returns before cache writes have completed
findings.description: Each cache.Set is scheduled with Task.Run but no task is awaited and exceptions are discarded. WarmCache can return with an empty or partially populated cache, contradicting its documented return-after-every-probe behavior.

findings.title: ProbeAsync never probes the target
findings.description: ProbeAsync only delays and then returns target.StartsWith('https://'). CheckTargets consequently reports every http:// target as a failure even though Store.Create explicitly accepts http:// URLs, and never detects an unreachable https:// target.

findings.title: CountForOwner throws for owners with no quota entry
findings.description: store.Quotas()[owner] uses the dictionary indexer. Owners that have never created a link have no entry, so a normal count query for a new or unknown owner throws KeyNotFoundException instead of returning zero.

findings.title: All responses are labeled application/json
findings.description: Respond sets Content-Type application/json for plain-text errors, the plain-text link listing, and CSV reports. Clients that honor the header parse valid CSV or text as JSON and fail.

findings.title: Store dictionaries are mutated by request tasks and the janitor without synchronization
findings.description: Main dispatches each HTTP request with Task.Run and also starts a Timer, so POST, DELETE, GET, stats, report and janitor work can all use the same Store at once. links and quota are plain Dictionary instances; All() and Quotas() return the live dictionaries. An interleaving such as Create executing links[code] = link while Page, TotalHits, SuccessRate, Prune or Worker.StartJanitor enumerates links.Keys, or a DELETE/Remove while the janitor indexes store.All()[code], can corrupt Dictionary bookkeeping, throw InvalidOperationException or KeyNotFoundException, and lose link or quota entries. Worker.StartJanitor also removes keys directly through the exposed dictionary.

findings.title: Store read-modify-write and multi-step operations are not atomic
findings.description: quota[owner] = quota[owner] + 1 is a non-atomic read-modify-write: once the owner key exists, two concurrent Create calls can both read N and write N+1, losing one quota increment. The same defect affects link.Hits++ at line 60, Rename's ContainsKey-to-Remove-to-Add sequence at lines 69-79 (two concurrent renames can overwrite one link), and ImportAll at lines 165-171 (other threads can observe a partial batch or interleave their writes). Concurrent stats and exports therefore report lost hits or inconsistent state.

findings.title: Concurrent link creation uses a shared non-thread-safe Random
findings.description: All Create calls invoke random.Next() on one System.Random instance. System.Random instance methods are not thread-safe; simultaneous POST /links requests can corrupt its seed state and return the same code (including repeated zero-like values). The second links[code] = link then silently overwrites the first link, so one owner loses their shortened link and both clients may receive the same code.

findings.title: Session store is unsynchronized and revocation has a TOCTOU window
findings.description: Issue writes sessions, Verify enumerates sessions.Values from concurrent HTTP request tasks, Revoke removes entries, and SessionCount reads the dictionary, all without a lock. A concurrent Issue can resize the dictionary while Verify is enumerating, causing InvalidOperationException or a missed valid session; concurrent Issue/Revoke can overwrite or remove the wrong session. Verify also returns the mutable Session object, so if Revoke runs after Verify but before Program.Handle dispatches the route, the in-flight request still proceeds with the revoked session despite the promise that revocation takes effect immediately.

findings.title: Shared Random can mint duplicate authentication tokens
findings.description: Issue generates tokens with two calls to a shared System.Random from whatever threads issue sessions. Concurrent calls can corrupt Random's internal state and produce identical token strings. Because sessions[session.Token] = session overwrites by key, the second Issue replaces the first session; one user's token can then verify as the other user's owner and role, including an admin or owner role.

findings.title: Cache methods that claim thread safety read shared state without the lock
findings.description: Get, Set, Delete and Sweep lock the instance, but Peek reads entries.ContainsKey, Stats reads the long hits field, and Utilization reads entries.Count without any synchronization. While a handler or warmer calls Set/Delete or the janitor calls Sweep, an unlocked ContainsKey/Count can race with Dictionary resizing or removal and return stale state or throw; Sweep's lock does not protect an unsynchronized reader. Stats can also observe a stale value or, on a 32-bit runtime, a torn long because hits++ is done under the lock but the read is not.

findings.title: HTTP handler tasks are fire-and-forget with no completion, cancellation or shutdown handling
findings.description: Every accepted context is passed to Task.Run and the returned Task is discarded. There is no await, exception handling, bounded concurrency, CancellationToken or drain path. If Handle throws before Respond (for example on a malformed Authorization header), the exception is only an unobserved Task exception and the response stream is never closed, leaving the client waiting. A burst of connections can queue unbounded work, and process shutdown cannot cancel or wait for in-flight handlers.

findings.title: WarmCache returns before its parallel work completes
findings.description: WarmCache starts a Task.Run for every link but neither stores nor awaits any Task; its synchronous void return contradicts the comment that it returns after every probe has finished. A caller invoking WarmCache and then reading the cache can see misses because the Set tasks have not run. Exceptions from cache.Set are unobserved, there is no cancellation, and the tasks read mutable Link fields after the caller may have modified them.

findings.title: Concurrent snapshots share one fixed temporary file
findings.description: Every WriteSnapshot call writes to /tmp/linkd-snapshot.json before moving it to snapshot.json. If two calls overlap, A can write payloadA, B can overwrite the same temp file with payloadB, A can move B's bytes into snapshot.json, and B's File.Move then fails because the temp file is gone. The resulting snapshot can contain the wrong payload while the other write is lost; concurrent moves to the same destination are also uncoordinated.

findings.title: Concurrent report requests with the same name write and read one shared file
findings.description: The /report endpoint derives the CSV path solely from the user-supplied name and Program.Report then calls ExportCsv followed by ReadReport on that same path. Two concurrent /report?name=x requests can open/truncate/write the same file at once: one can get a sharing IOException, one can read the other's partially written or empty report, and sequential overlap can make the first response return bytes written by the second request. The response is therefore a 500, a truncated report, or another request's report.

findings.title: Warm has a check-then-act race that can overwrite a fresh cache entry with stale data
findings.description: Warm performs an unlocked Peek and a later separate locked Set. If the janitor sees a code absent, a handler then calls Set with the current target, and the janitor subsequently calls Set with its warmed value, the stale value overwrites the current entry. Two concurrent Warm loops can similarly overwrite each other's values. A cached code can then resolve to the wrong target.

findings.title: Metrics created counter uses a non-atomic increment and unsynchronized snapshots
findings.description: Multiple POST /links handler tasks can call AddCreated simultaneously; created++ is read-modify-write, so two increments can collapse into one. Snapshot reads resolved, created and errors with plain field reads; even the Interlocked-updated resolved long can be stale or torn on a 32-bit runtime without Interlocked.Read/Volatile.Read. The dashboard consequently loses created-link counts and can display inconsistent counters.

findings.title: Repeated janitor starts leak Timers and allow overlapping callbacks
findings.description: StartJanitor assigns a new Timer to the static janitor field without disposing the previous one. If it is called again during reconfiguration or in tests, both timers keep running; StopJanitor only disposes the most recent Timer, so old callbacks and captured Store/Cache objects remain indefinitely. System.Threading.Timer callbacks can also overlap when a tick runs long, and these callbacks enumerate and mutate the shared Store without a reentrancy guard.

findings.title: CheckTargets blocks on async probes and can deadlock under a synchronization context
findings.description: ProbeAsync awaits Task.Delay(1) without ConfigureAwait(false), while CheckTargets blocks the calling thread on ProbeAsync(...).Result. If CheckTargets is invoked on a single-threaded SynchronizationContext, the continuation is posted back to that blocked context and cannot complete, deadlocking the call. Even on the thread pool it blocks a worker for each probe and offers no CancellationToken or way for concurrent callers to cancel, which can starve the pool under load.

findings.title: Concurrent audit appends are not coordinated
findings.description: AppendAudit calls File.AppendAllText on the same path with no lock or retry. File.AppendAllText opens the file for write while only sharing read access; if two request or background threads append at the same time, the second call can fail with an IOException and lose its audit event, or overlapping platform writes can interleave partial lines. The method's open-and-close design provides no serialization across callers.

findings.title: ExportCsvAsync is async void fire-and-forget
findings.description: The background exporter cannot await ExportCsvAsync, observe when its File.WriteAllTextAsync finishes, cancel it, or catch its IOException. The process can exit while the write is still in flight, and an async void exception is unobserved or rethrown on a synchronization context. Concurrent calls with the same name also target the same file with no coordination.

findings.title: Stats takes multiple unsynchronized Store views and can divide by zero
findings.description: Stats evaluates TotalHits(), Count, SuccessRate() and other state in separate Store calls. If the janitor or a concurrent DELETE removes the last link after TotalHits() has enumerated a nonempty dictionary but before Count is read, Count is zero and TotalHits() / store.Count throws DivideByZeroException; because Handle is an unobserved Task, the response is never closed. Other interleavings produce hits-per-link and success-rate values from different Store states.

findings.title: FollowedSummary enumerates a live dictionary-backed query twice
findings.description: Store.Followed() returns a deferred LINQ query over links.Values, and FollowedSummary enumerates it once for Count() and again for FirstOrDefault(). A concurrent Create, Delete or janitor removal between those enumerations invalidates the Dictionary enumerator, causing InvalidOperationException on the second enumeration or reporting a count from one Store state and a first link from another.

findings.title: User-controlled report names escape the export directory
findings.description: ExportCsv combines the caller's name with the export directory and appends .csv without verifying it is a plain filename. An absolute name or ../ sequences makes Path.Combine ignore or traverse the configured root; the StreamWriter then creates or truncates that file, and ReadReport reads it back. ArchiveAll's entry.Key and ExportCsvAsync have the same defect. An authenticated /report request can overwrite any service-writable .csv file outside ExportDir and read files outside the intended directory.

findings.title: DELETE /links ignores the authenticated owner
findings.description: Handle verifies a session, but Links does not receive it; DELETE calls store.Delete with only the client-supplied code. Store.Delete removes any matching link with no ownership or role check. An authenticated user who learns another user's code through the predictable code generator or the all-owner report can permanently delete that user's link.

findings.title: Fixed /tmp snapshot path allows symlink overwrite
findings.description: WriteSnapshot always writes to /tmp/linkd-snapshot.json in a world-writable directory. A local attacker can pre-create that path as a symlink to a service-writable file; File.WriteAllText follows the symlink and truncates the target with snapshot payload before File.Move moves the symlink into the export directory. This permits arbitrary file corruption with the service account's privileges.

findings.title: Bearer tokens and reports are served over plaintext HTTP on all interfaces
findings.description: The listener binds http://*:<port>/, so Authorization bearer tokens and CSV reports containing every owner's links traverse the network unencrypted. A passive observer on the LAN or an upstream network can capture a token from any request and replay it against /links, /report, and /admin/quotas.

findings.title: All-owner reports are created with default, potentially world-readable permissions
findings.description: The comment says the report must be readable only by the service user, but new StreamWriter(path) creates the file subject only to the process umask. Under a common 022 umask, /var/lib/linkd/exports/report.csv is mode 0644, so any local unprivileged user can read all owners, codes, targets, and hit counts after /report is used. ArchiveAll and WriteSnapshot similarly set no restrictive mode.

findings.title: Admin quota endpoint trusts a client-supplied X-Admin header
findings.description: AdminQuotas checks context.Request.Headers['X-Admin'] == 'true' instead of the verified session's server-side role. Any authenticated non-admin can add X-Admin: true to a request for /admin/quotas and pass the administrator-only authorization check.

findings.title: RequireAdmin authorizes every non-admin role
findings.description: The false branch of the allowed-role check returns true, so RequireAdmin('user'), RequireAdmin('guest'), and any other role are treated as administrators. Any admin-only code path that uses this intended helper grants privilege escalation.

findings.title: POST /links lets the caller spoof another owner
findings.description: The owner used by Store.Create comes from the query string rather than session.Owner. Any authenticated caller can create links attributed to an arbitrary owner, poisoning ownership records and quotas and bypassing any downstream owner-scoped access control.

findings.title: Report endpoint discloses every owner's links to any authenticated user
findings.description: Report calls store.Page(0, 1000), which includes all owners' codes, targets, owners, and hit counts, then streams the resulting CSV back. There is no filter by session.Owner and no administrator check, so any token can harvest sensitive short links belonging to all users.

findings.title: Unvalidated /out Location enables phishing through a trusted domain
findings.description: The next query parameter is copied directly into a 301 Location header without an origin or scheme allowlist. An attacker can send a victim a URL on the trusted linkd domain such as /out?next=https://attacker.example/login; the browser immediately redirects to the attacker's site, making credential theft look like a link from the trusted service. The /l endpoint similarly accepts any target merely beginning with http:// or https://.

findings.title: Session bearer tokens are generated with a non-cryptographic PRNG
findings.description: Issue concatenates two outputs of a shared System.Random instance. The resulting token has at most the entropy of Random's 32-bit seed and follows a predictable PRNG sequence rather than a CSPRNG. An attacker who observes a token from logs, a proxy, or a leaked request can infer the generator state and predict subsequent tokens, then impersonate their owners, including admins.

findings.title: Session bearer tokens are written to stdout
findings.description: Issue prints the full token and owner to Console.Anyone with access to container logs, journald, or centralized log storage can copy the credential and replay it in an Authorization header; because Verify does not enforce expiry, the stolen token remains usable until explicitly revoked.

findings.title: Verify ignores session expiry
findings.description: Verify returns any matching token without comparing Session.ExpiresAt to the current time. A token issued for 12 hours, leaked from logs, or stolen from an old request remains valid indefinitely; expiration cannot revoke access and Revoke is the only effective invalidation.

findings.title: ByOwner uses substring matching and leaks other owners' links
findings.description: The filter l.Owner.Contains(owner) treats the requested owner as a substring rather than an identity. ByOwner('a') returns links owned by alice, bank, mallory, and others whose names contain a; any owner-scoped listing built on this method exposes unrelated users' links.

findings.title: Short codes are predictable
findings.description: NewCode returns one Random.Next value as an eight-character hex code. The code space is small and generated by a non-cryptographic PRNG shared across all links, so an attacker who observes one code can predict or brute-force other codes and use the unauthenticated-by-owner DELETE path or global report to access links they do not own.

findings.title: Hardcoded fallback shared secret
findings.description: When LINKD_SECRET is unset, Authenticator.Secret exposes the source-known value dev-secret-do-not-use. Any integration that uses this public secret with SecretEquals to authenticate administrative or webhook requests will accept the known constant in a deployment that forgot the environment variable.

findings.title: Passwords are hashed with unsalted fast SHA-256
findings.description: HashPassword applies one unkeyed SHA-256 pass with no per-user salt or work factor. If the user table or a backup leaks, an attacker can use precomputed rainbow tables and high-rate GPU dictionary attacks to recover common passwords and reuse them against this or other services.

findings.title: Shared-secret comparison is not constant time
findings.description: SecretEquals uses ordinary string ==, which short-circuits at the first differing character. An attacker who can submit many candidate secrets through a caller of this public helper and measure response timing can recover the expected secret prefix by prefix. Verify's token equality has the same early-exit property.

findings.title: CSV fields are not escaped, allowing formula and row injection
findings.description: Code, target, owner, and hits are interpolated directly into CSV. Targets and owners can contain commas, quotes, embedded newlines, and leading =, +, -, or @ characters. When support opens the /report output in a spreadsheet, attacker-controlled formulas or extra rows can execute commands or exfiltrate spreadsheet data.

findings.title: Audit log entries can be forged with unescaped newlines
findings.description: AppendAudit writes the caller's line followed by a newline without escaping. If any attacker-controlled owner, target, or code contains newline characters, it creates additional audit records, letting an attacker hide an action or forge entries attributed to administrators.

findings.title: Create-link response injects unescaped target into JSON
findings.description: The POST /links response interpolates link.Target directly into a JSON string. Store.Create only requires an http:// or https:// prefix, so a target containing quotes, control characters, or JSON syntax produces malformed JSON or extra attacker-controlled properties for downstream API clients.

findings.title: Verbose exception details are returned to clients
findings.description: The /report IOException handler returns cfg.ExportDir and e.ToString() in the HTTP body. By forcing an export failure with a crafted name, a client can obtain absolute filesystem paths, exception messages, and stack-trace details useful for locating writable paths and fingerprinting the deployment.

findings.title: Mutable internal quota and link dictionaries are exposed
findings.description: Quotas returns the live quota dictionary despite claiming to be a snapshot, and All at line 208 returns the live links dictionary. Any caller with a Store reference can set arbitrary quotas or replace a code with a Link whose target and owner were never validated, bypassing quota controls and poisoning redirects.

findings.title: Expiry comparison is reversed, so expired links can still resolve
findings.description: Resolve removes and rejects a link when DateTime.Now < link.ExpiresAt, i.e. while it is still valid, but returns the target once that time has passed. Until the janitor happens to delete it, an expired short link remains usable; Extend can also revive an expired link. This defeats link TTLs used to limit access to sensitive destinations.

findings.title: Malformed Authorization input aborts request handling
findings.description: BearerToken indexes parts[1] without checking length or the Bearer scheme. A request with no Authorization header or a single-word value throws IndexOutOfRangeException; Handle has no catch, so no 401 is written and OutputStream is never closed. The same unhandled-exception pattern applies to int.Parse on ttl, offset, and size at Program.cs lines 90, 119, and 120, allowing repeated malformed requests to tie up connections and workers.

findings.title: Invalid runtime configuration is accepted
findings.description: Validate collects problems but always returns true, and Program.Main ignores its result. For example, LINKD_CACHE_SIZE=0 starts the server and makes /stats call Cache.Utilization's division by zero; LINKD_TIMEOUT_MS=bad sets a zero timeout and still starts. An operator cannot rely on startup validation to prevent unsafe or denial-of-service-prone configurations.
